elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy liability; no commercial general liability coverage is required anywhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No CGL aggregate limit appears; the insertion states only "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O is set at "not less than USD 1,000,000", which is the fallback amount and below the preferred USD 2,000,000 threshold.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Licensor operates the Platform and routes Customer trading/market data, so the condition applies, but the cyber and privacy limit is "not less than USD 2,000,000", below USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation covenant appears in the inserted clause or elsewhere in the rendered General Provisions.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: No certificate-of-insurance delivery mechanic is included; the insertion ends after the two coverage limits.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000" — correct party direction (Licensor is the counterparty), correct coverage type and amount floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: "...and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000" — express cyber/privacy coverage at the fallback floor.

reasons: The rule is correctly scored as missing: the Agreement's only prior use of "insurance" is a pass-through of taxes/customs/duties/insurance charges payable by Licensee, and the General Provisions article (governing law through representation by counsel) contains no insurance covenant. A concise insertion is the appropriate remedy and all-new wording does not defeat minimality for a missing clause.

Both fallback elements are met in operative language with the obligation placed on Licensor (counterparty alias) and stated as floors ("not less than"), so the fallback checklist is position-complete.

Preferred level is not complete: CGL per-occurrence and aggregate limits, workers' compensation, and certificates on request are entirely absent, and the E&O (USD 1M vs 2M) and cyber (USD 2M vs 5M) amounts sit below the preferred thresholds. This is acceptable as a deliberate fallback landing, not a defect, but the drafter should not describe the result as preferred.

Minimality holds: the drafter omitted the model-language extras (at-own-expense, throughout-the-term-plus-one-year survival tail, CGL, certificates), added no procedure or notice mechanic outside the two selected elements, and deleted nothing from the retained General Provisions text, including subsection (k), which survives verbatim.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is additive, creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the retained fee/tax pass-through reference to insurance charges payable by Licensee, which addresses shipping-type charges rather than a coverage covenant.

Drafting nit only, not a scoring defect: the rationale describes the insertion as new General Provisions subsection (l), but the rendered text carries the heading "INSURANCE." without the (l) enumerator; align the lettering with the surrounding (a)-(k) scheme before sending.
